words: Stenger argues satellite measurements put cosmic energy density at critical density, consistent with an initial zero-energy state, so cosmic formation requires no divine energy input.
critique: Strongest feature: Stenger connects satellite measurements placing average cosmic energy density at critical density with an initial zero-energy state, supporting the inference that cosmic formation needs no external energy or miraculous creation. Principal limitation: Critical-density agreement is compatible with zero total energy, yet the excerpt presents compatibility as confirmation, neglects rival cosmological interpretations, and overextends physical sufficiency into an inactive-deity conclusion. Live burden: He must establish why measured density confirms the proposed initial state, explain how zero net energy produces ordered expansion, and exclude active divine causation rather than merely remove an energy-source puzzle. Locked score: The exact score of 67 fits because responsiveness strongly confronts creation from nothing, whereas weaker evidence warrant and calibration charity reflect unsupported cosmological and theological certainty.
